rules.when: The task is a trivial mechanical edit: a rote rename, a formatting sweep, a typo or copy fix, a version bump, or gathering files and facts with no judgment involved.
rules.why: Narrow, low-ambiguity work. The cheapest fast profile is enough, and the crew plugins are installed for Claude Code only.

rules.when: The task is read-only and plans or reports rather than changes code: a scout investigation other than a bug diagnosis (a bug scout falls under the bug rule below), a UX review of existing UI, a QA test plan or acceptance check, backlog refinement, sprint planning, triaging why a CI run failed, or drafting a backlog or board plan.
rules.why: Reading and judging, not building: /designer:review, /qa:plan and /qa:verify (which comments its verdict and moves the card, but never changes code), /scrum-master:refine and plan-sprint, and /devops:triage as a scout, all run well on Sonnet.

rules.when: The task reviews a pull request's code: a /code-reviewer:review of a PR the developer shipped, or a re-review after a fix push.
rules.why: Judging, not building, but a missed defect reaches QA and the Captain: /code-reviewer:review runs its passes in fresh reviewer subagents and must prove every finding with a failure scenario, which needs the stronger model. It posts a PR review and may move the card to In progress, but never changes code.

rules.when: The task is a bug whose cause is not known yet: a crash, wrong output, a failing or flaky test, or a regression that has to be diagnosed or bisected before it can be fixed.
rules.why: /developer:diagnose must prove a mechanism before any fix, and /developer:bisect reads the culprit commit. A wrong diagnosis costs more than the extra effort.

rules.when: The task is a large or ambiguous multi-file feature, a risky refactor, or a change touching migrations, auth, payments, data deletion or a public contract.
rules.why: Many moving parts and costly mistakes: the strongest profile, and the Captain confirms the dispatch.

rules.when: The task deploys or sets up a deploy: PR preview environments, a deploy job, a hosting provider, or anything that needs secrets added to a repository.
rules.why: /devops:preview and deploy work touch hosting accounts and secrets, which only the Captain can add, and the proof is a live deploy. The Captain confirms the dispatch. CI setup without a deploy, and /devops:triage, need no approval.

rules.when: The task builds or changes UI: a new screen, page, flow or component that needs a /designer:spec first and a /designer:review before pushing.
rules.why: Spec, implement and review in one session. Every state, the copy and accessibility have to hold together.
